meta.title: Trade and foreign capital
meta.question: Should Poland protect its economy from foreign competition and capital?
meta.measure: Average position on trade and foreign capital, from 0 (free trade) to 10 (protection)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on foreign capital, on selling firms and land to foreigners and on protecting domestic producers, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Foreigners should not be allowed to buy land in Poland (agree-disagree)
Poland should limit the import of foreign products in order to protect its national economy (agree-disagree)
Is the presence of foreign capital good or bad for the Polish economy?
Is foreign capital's share in the Polish economy too small, about right or too large?
State enterprises should be sold above all to Polish investors vs to whichever investors offer most
It does not matter whether capital is Polish or foreign vs the inflow of foreign capital should be limited, 0-10
Free inflow of foreign capital (0) vs limiting the inflow of foreign capital (10)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study; the PGSW_FOREIGN_CAP question.

items.wording: Are the growing trade and business ties between Poland and other countries a very good ... very bad thing for our country?
items.notes: Pew 2002, 2007, 2008, spring 2009, 2010, 2011, 2014, 2018 (8). The regex leaves out the follow-up about 'you and your family'.

items.wording: Does foreign capital have decisively too much ... decisively too little power in Poland?
Should foreign capital be allowed to set up large enterprises?
Should selling state enterprises to foreign capital be allowed?
Does the term 'free trade' bring to mind something very positive ... very negative?
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer 2005-22, 16 waves. Concept images share a general positivity (most terms' images correlate positively, up to 0.5, whatever their politics), but free trade relates as expected to 'globalisation is an opportunity' (0.13-0.31).

items.wording: Is globalisation a good opportunity for Polish companies thanks to the opening-up of markets, or a threat to employment and companies in Poland?
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, 6 waves: September 2006, March and October 2008, June and October 2009, May 2012. In 2008 a Turkish Cypriot copy matches too but comes second.

items.wording: Globalisation is an opportunity for economic growth (tend to agree / tend to disagree)
items.notes: Eurobarometer 76.3 (November 2011) only, two-point (label misspelt by GESIS); its Turkish Cypriot copy comes second.

items.wording: Globalisation is an opportunity for economic growth (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer May 2012 - 2021, 20 waves. Each wave also has a copy for the Turkish Cypriot community, which matches the regex but comes second, so the general question is used. Globalisation in general, not trade alone.

items.wording: When foreign companies buy Polish companies, does this have a very good ... very bad impact on our country?
When foreign companies build new factories in Poland, does this have a very good ... very bad impact?
Trade liberalisation (0) vs protection of domestic producers (10)
Free trade and openness to foreign investment benefit the whole of society even if some local communities must adjust (1) vs protecting jobs and local communities comes first (7)
items.notes: Postliberalism survey (2025, provisional date). The eight statement pairs share their value labels, so the variable label picks the question.
